---
title: "The retreat itself and after"
unit: 5
module: 4
duration: "10 min"
---

<Phase type="activation">

Picture a logbook after a flight. The plane is at the stand, the passengers have gone. The pilot sits down and writes what did not go to plan in the air.

**The flight is over, the logbook is not.** Think about what from your retreat is worth writing down while the memory is fresh.

</Phase>

<Phase type="reflection">

Go back to the logbook. It is written not for a report but for the next flight.

**A retreat does not end on the day of departure.** A review afterwards turns one week into experience the next one is built on.

</Phase>

<Phase type="concept">

## Costs on site

During a retreat, spending appears that was not in the plan: phone and data, an extra transfer, replacing broken equipment, a gift for a guest. They are worth writing down straight away, one line in your phone.

## Plan versus actual

A few days after the retreat, open the calculator with your original numbers. Enter the actual ones: how many guests came, what the costs were, how much went to the venue. Compare the honest profit of the plan and of the actual. In the [teaching deal](https://academy.synergify.com/en/instrumenty/kalkulyator-retrita/#) from 01/u2, with 18 guests instead of 20 it falls from 22,200 to 16,380 dollars.

The difference shows which line you got wrong. It is the most useful number for the next price.

## A conversation with the venue

A short review with the venue after the group helps both sides. What worked and what did not: the kitchen, the halls, meeting the guests, the dates. It is also the time to ask about terms for next time.

## Guests after the retreat

It is worth writing to guests a few days later: thanks, materials, a request for feedback. Feedback is not advertising but information: what mattered most to the person.

## Terms for next time

The result of the review is three terms you will change in the next contract or guest terms. For example: a different payment schedule, an earlier deadline for the final guest count, a bigger transfer reserve.

<SelfCheck id="c5"/>

</Phase>

<Phase type="practice">

1. Open the calculator with your retreat's original numbers. To practise, take the [teaching deal](https://academy.synergify.com/en/instrumenty/kalkulyator-retrita/#) as the plan.
2. Enter the actual number of guests and all actual costs.
3. Write down the difference in honest profit between plan and actual, and the line that caused most of it.
4. Write down three questions for the venue for the review after the group.
5. Write down three terms you will change in the next contract or guest terms.

</Phase>
